dataFlow: When a shopper visits a sold-out product page the widget calls GET /widget/availability to determine whether to render (suppressed on in-stock items) and GET /widget/signup to surface any existing signup for that email+item. The shopper submits their email via POST /widget/signup, which is deduplicated and stored as an active waitlist entry with a queue position. When inventory rises above zero (inventory_levels/update webhook fires), the backend resolves the affected variant via the inventoryItem admin query, identifies all active waitlist entries for that variant ordered by queue position, and opens a restock event — it then fans out notification emails up to the available quantity and marks each notified entry as notified, leaving the rest active for the next restock. When an order is paid (orders/paid webhook), the backend checks whether any notified waitlist entry for that customer email and any purchased variant falls within the 7-day conversion window and records it as converted. When a product is deleted (products/delete webhook), all waitlist entries for that product are immediately purged. The merchant uses the admin dashboard to see a queue-size ranking, drill into per-product subscriber lists, export CSV, edit the email template, and configure quiet hours.

triggers.event: inventory level for a variant rises above zero
triggers.idempotency: if a restock event already exists for the same inventory item external id within the same restock window (available went from zero to positive without returning to zero in between), do not open a second event

payloadBindings.resolution: resolve variant id from inventory_item_id via the inventoryItem admin GraphQL query (inventoryItem.variant.id)

triggers.idempotency: deletion is idempotent — purging an already-purged product's entries is a no-op

triggers.event: a customer completes a paid order
triggers.idempotency: if a conversion record already exists for this order external id, treat the event as a no-op

persistence.name: waitlist_entries
persistence.purpose: Stores every shopper signup for a sold-out item, tracks queue position, notification status, and conversion.

columns.name: item_external_id
columns.purpose: the variant or product external id the shopper is waiting on; combined with item_scope to determine the level of the signup

columns.name: item_scope
columns.purpose: discriminates between a variant-level and a product-level signup

columns.name: product_external_id
columns.purpose: always the parent product id; used to purge all entries on products/delete without a join

columns.name: queue_position
columns.purpose: monotonically increasing integer within each item, used to fan out notifications in sign-up order

columns.name: status
columns.purpose: lifecycle: active, notified, converted, unsubscribed, purged

columns.name: unsubscribe_token
columns.purpose: single-use opaque token embedded in every notification email for one-click global unsubscribe

columns.name: restock_event_id
columns.purpose: set when the entry is notified; references the restock_events row that triggered the notification so per-restock dedup is enforced

queryPatterns: active entries for a given item_external_id ordered by queue_position ascending (notification fan-out)
all entries for a given product_external_id (bulk purge on deletion)
single entry by email and item_external_id (dedup check on signup)
all active entries for a given email (global unsubscribe)
entries for a given item_external_id filtered by status with cursor pagination (admin drill-in)
entries with status=notified and email matching a paid-order's contact email within 7 days of notified_at (conversion matching)

persistence.name: restock_events
persistence.purpose: Records each distinct restock event for an item so the system knows which entries have already been notified for a given restock and prevents duplicate blasts.

columns.name: item_external_id
columns.purpose: the variant or product external id that was restocked

columns.name: item_scope
columns.purpose: discriminates variant-level vs product-level, mirrors waitlist_entries.item_scope

columns.name: inventory_item_external_id
columns.purpose: the inventory item id from the webhook, used for idempotency keying

columns.name: available_quantity
columns.purpose: units available at the moment the restock was detected; governs how many waitlist positions to notify

columns.name: notification_budget
columns.purpose: number of entries authorised to be notified in this event; computed as min(available_quantity, active_waitlist_count)

columns.name: notified_count
columns.purpose: running count of entries actually notified in this event; incremented as emails are dispatched

columns.name: status
columns.purpose: open, dispatching, completed

queryPatterns: latest open or dispatching event for a given item_external_id (idempotency check on new inventory_levels/update)
single event by id (update notified_count and status)

persistence.name: conversion_records
persistence.purpose: Records confirmed conversions where a notified shopper purchased the item within the 7-day window.

columns.name: waitlist_entry_id
columns.purpose: the waitlist entry that was credited with the conversion

columns.name: order_external_id
columns.purpose: the paid order that triggered the conversion check; used for idempotency

queryPatterns: lookup by order_external_id (idempotency on duplicate orders/paid delivery)

persistence.name: notification_settings
persistence.purpose: Merchant-configured email template and quiet-hours window; singleton row.

columns.name: id
columns.purpose: singleton row guard; code enforces at most one row

columns.name: email_body
columns.purpose: merchant-authored template supporting {{product_name}}, {{item_details}}, and {{unsubscribe_url}} tokens

columns.name: quiet_hours_start
columns.purpose: hour-of-day (0–23) at which quiet hours begin; no notifications sent in the quiet window

columns.name: quiet_hours_end
columns.purpose: hour-of-day (0–23) at which quiet hours end

queryPatterns: single row read before every notification dispatch to check quiet hours and render template

edgeCases: Duplicate inventory_levels/update deliveries for the same inventory item with available > 0 — check for an open or dispatching restock event for that inventory item before creating a new one; second delivery is a no-op.

Stock rises, notifications go out, stock immediately sells through and rises again — the second rise creates a new restock event with a new notification budget; entries that were already notified in the first event are eligible for the second only if their status is still active (not yet converted or unsubscribed).
Quiet hours are active when notifications are ready to dispatch — hold the entire batch until the quiet window ends; do not send partial batches that straddle the boundary.
Duplicate orders/paid delivery for the same order external id — the conversion_records unique key on (waitlist_entry_id, order_external_id) makes the upsert idempotent; no double-credit.
Shopper has no email address on the paid order — skip conversion matching for that order, record the gap in an edge log, do not crash the handler.
products/delete fires for a product that has no waitlist entries — purge is a no-op; do not return an error.

Notification email delivery fails for one entry in a batch — log the failure and continue dispatching remaining entries; do not roll back the entire restock event; failed entries remain in notified status so the merchant can diagnose via the admin drill-in.

Same email signs up for the same item a second time (e.g. after a previous unsubscribe) — the unique key on (email, item_external_id) blocks a duplicate insert; return already_signed_up flag to the widget.
